direction_as_read: Positive on named primary cough outcomes for the EA 575 extract at 105 mg/day in maker-funded placebo trials; an independent systematic review calls the effects minimal at best and of uncertain clinical importance
summary: All four labels print generic English ivy leaf extract, 50 mg or 86 mg, with no extract name or ratio; the rows carry an immune purpose, and two also carry an infant tag. Maker-funded placebo trials of EA 575 liquid in adults found primary cough outcomes favored the extract (29441845, 31832428), with a two-trial meta-analysis confirming it (36414647). A systematic review of ivy leaf preparations rated risk of bias high and called effects minimal at best and of uncertain clinical importance (33523253).
question_for_clinician: 31832428 and 36414647 meet rule 2 for EA 575 at 105 mg/day, positive on the primary outcome, and 29441845 does too except for an amount in its abstract. Should these labels get credit, given they print a generic extract with no ratio, at 50 or 86 mg, an immune purpose rather than a cough purpose, and an infant tag on two labels, while the trials tested one liquid extract in adults, with maker funding? Agent recommendation: no credit in this review, because the labels can't be shown to contain the tested extract.
